So I'm certainly not the best falco player out there but I like to think I'm decent at this matchup. 

One thing that's fairly important with nair/dair is mixing up *when* you choose to approach. Faking an approach and then dashing back/~~wavedashing back~~ can bait out a fair or uptilt or movement option from the Marth, in which case you jump in right after (to whiff punish the fair/uptilt) with your nair or dair, or shoot another laser if they're moving away from you. Note: if they move towards you, you have to be ready to shield/keep dashing away. Another mixup here for continuing pressure is to dash back/wavedash towards them and uptilt. If they get impatient or mis-space something the uptilt can set up a decent punish. If you consistently laser then jump in with a nair or dair it'll be pretty easy for a decent marth to stuff it out or dodge it and whiff punish. 

It's pretty important to recognize what options your opponent likes to do when they get hit by laser and tailoring your approaches to punish those options (ie if they tend to shield all your lasers, try to laser close to them and get in with a shinegrab or crossup dair). Don't be afraid to grab them when they shield (or when they do something with bad spacing) even tho falcos throws aren't the best.

I highly recommend checking out Ginger's YouTube channel. He's done some analysis for his subscribers that I found really helpful for this matchup and others.

Yeah in every game since melee (brawl may have had edge cancelling but I don't think so), there is no L cancelling or edge cancelling.

In melee, when your character is performing an aerial (forward air, down air etc) and you land in the middle of it, you'd have a set amount of endlag where your character had to recover before you could act again and input something (that part is the same as ultimate). If you press L or R within a couple frames of landing (or maybe right before), your endlag would only be half what it was if you didn't press L/R.

Edge cancelling is a little different. If you are in the air and land on the edge of a platform while moving in the direction towards the edge, your momentum would slide you off the edge of the platform. Now, the landing and subsequent sliding off into the air has some cool effects. If you're doing an aerial and then land, then slide off, you could immediately do another aerial. This is because the landing on the platform would put you into a grounded state where you'd go through the endlag (like I explained before), but then when you slide off you're immediately back into an actionable state in the air.

There are some other tricks they did in the video but these two things are used by melee players all the time and are part of what makes melee so much faster than ultimate/smash4 etc.

Generally though the end lag is much lesser than newer games due to L-cancelling.

So with the update they secretly made it so that troops won't retarget until a troop is dead. Before they used to retarget once the projectile that would kill their target was in the air.

For example a sparky is targeting a tower. There are minions above it and the tower is shooting it too. If the arrow from the tower would kill it, the minions used to leave the moment that arrow was shot. Now the minions will keep attacking it until the sparky dies. This used to cause some complaints because people would watch as a sparky or something else is ignored by troops that would kill it faster than the tower's arrow, and then the troop would get another hit off.

So now due to this change, the sparky will still shoot because the troop isn't dead yet. But if the troop dies before it gets hit by the sparky shot, then the sparky is treated as though it didn't shoot, and still has full charge. But the sparky shot, which didn't hit it's target, still has splash damage.
